image_description: Two men kneeling in shallow river water holding a large sturgeon horizontally. The background features a rocky, vegetated riverbank. The sturgeon is the central subject, displaying characteristic bony scutes along its lateral line and back.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Elongated head with protrusible mouth on ventral surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is visible but the angle and resolution obscure the ventral mouth structure; it appears more terminal than clearly ventral/protrusible due to image quality.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Four barbels (sensory whiskers) anterior to mouth.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The underside of the snout where barbels are located is occluded by the angle of the fish and the holder's hand/arm position, making them impossible to verify.
The snout is clearly visible and exhibits the characteristic pointed, paddle-like shape of a sturgeon.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Elongated fusiform body with impressively large, extended proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The fish displays a clear elongated, torpedo-shaped body consistent with sturgeon morphology.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Five rows of bony scutes (plates) along body instead of scales.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Distinct rows of bony plates (scutes) are clearly visible running longitudinally along the dorsal and lateral aspects of the fish.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Gray, brown, or black dorsally with lighter ventral surface.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal side is grayish-brown while the visible lower flank transitions to a lighter white/cream color.
The tail fin is visible on the right side and shows the characteristic asymmetry where the upper lobe is larger than the lower lobe.
